value.text:
Informational advisory: Session upload progress

News Archive - 2026

Here are the most important news items we have published in 2026 on PHP.net.

We suggest you set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the
next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector.
This setting was already listed as a mitigation in the
GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp
advisory for CVE-2026-109619 published on Oct 21st, 2026. If you applied it
then, keep it in place and no further action is needed.

The issue can only occur under an unusual combination of configuration and
application code. An application must set
session.serialize_handler to php_binary or
php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to
php at runtime with ini_set() before calling
session_start(). Session upload progress must also still be
enabled. Applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime can
keep the feature enabled. Since this setup is unlikely in practice, we are
handling it in the regular release cycle and will publish a full advisory for
CVE-2026-115560 with the next release.

PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately.

Who is at risk: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.

The vulnerabilities:

RCE via OOM corruption, CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w): out-of-memory
handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid.

RCE via stale global state, CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp): request-owned
internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it.

How to update:

Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Source downloads are on our downloads page. Windows source and binaries are on the same page.

Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance, so check your vendor for updated packages.

PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project. Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor for details, or upgrade to a supported version.

Given the severity of these vulnerabilities, the PHP security team provided minimal source-backports for PHP 7.4, PHP 8.0, and PHP 8.1 to help people building from source or without access to an LTS vendor.

If you cannot update immediately: while only an update is a complete solution, the following measures reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe.

RCE via OOM corruption (CVE-2026-109618):

Set memory_limit=-1, preferably in a way applications can't override, such as php_admin_value in the FPM pool or Apache configuration, and check that no pool, directory or application setting puts a finite limit back. This removes the controllable PHP memory limit failure, but an underlying allocation failure can still reach the vulnerable path.

Set a low post_max_size. For applications that don't require file uploads, set post_max_size = 8M. If file uploads are necessary, set post_max_size = 32M. Keep upload_max_filesize below post_max_size.
Consider enforcing limits at the web server or proxy level for decoded request size, input field count, multipart part count, header count, and nesting depth. These
limits must also cover requests without a usable Content-Length.

Use a container or cgroup limit as an availability boundary, preferably with a policy that kills only the affected worker. Do not substitute RLIMIT_AS or
RLIMIT_DATA, as these can cause the vulnerable allocation failure.

RCE via stale global state (CVE-2026-109619):

Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restart every worker. Use php.ini, an FPM pool or server
configuration that applies before request parsing. Do not rely on ini_set() or FPM .user.ini. This blocks the confirmed session paths but not other variants.

On PHP 8.5, set fatal_error_backtraces=0 and restart every worker. This blocks the confirmed fatal backtrace path only.

Remove invalid or deprecated settings applied per request that emit diagnostics before initialization. Hiding diagnostics with error_reporting, display_errors
or @ does not help.

Fix attacker-reachable fatal errors and execution timeouts, including failures in callbacks, upload or import processing and cleanup.

The advisories linked above have the full technical details.

The PHP team is pleased to announce the third release candidate of PHP 8.6.0, RC4. This continues the PHP 8.6 release cycle, whose rough outline is specified in the PHP Wiki.

Source downloads of PHP 8.6.0 RC4 are available on the download page.

Please carefully test this version and report any issues found in the GitHub Issues.

This version also contains the fixes for two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Everyone running earlier builds of PHP 8.6.0 is strongly encouraged to update immediately.

Please DO NOT use this version in production, it is an early test version.

For more information on the new features and other changes, you can read the NEWS file, or the UPGRADING file for a complete list of upgrading notes. These files can also be found in the release archive.

The next release will be the last release candidate (RC5), planned for 5 November 2026.

The signatures for the release can be found in the manifest or on the pre-release builds page.

Thank you for helping us make PHP better.

The PHP security team would like to give advance notice of an
upcoming security release.

It is scheduled for Wednesday, 21 October 2026 at 14:00 UTC.

It addresses two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2.

All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as
soon as the release is available.

We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either
vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation
appear in the wild.

Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be
published with the release.

Thank you for helping us keep PHP secure.

The State of PHP survey is still open, but not for much longer. It asks how PHP is working for you: what you build with, what is painful, and what you think PHP should focus on next. It takes around 15 minutes.

The survey is run by The PHP Foundation in partnership with PhpStorm by JetBrains.

The aggregated results will be published later this year as the State of PHP 2026 report. The anonymized raw dataset will be released along with it, so anyone in the community can check the numbers or run their own analysis.

More responses mean a better picture of what matters to PHP users. If you have not filled it in yet, please do, and share it with your colleagues and user groups.

The International PHP Conference
is the world's first PHP conference and has stood for more than two decades for top-notch
pragmatic expertise in PHP and web technologies. At the IPC, internationally renowned
experts from the PHP industry meet up with PHP users and developers from large and small
companies. Here is the place where concepts emerge and ideas are born – the IPC signifies
knowledge transfer at the highest level.

Basic facts:

Date: October 26 – 30, 2026

Location: Holiday Inn Munich City Centre, Munich or Online

Highlights:

60+ best practice sessions

50+ international top speakers

PHPower: Hands-on Power Workshops

2-Day Bootcamp on Thursday and Friday

Expo with exciting exhibitors on October 27 & 28

All inclusive: Changing buffets, snacks & refreshing drinks

Official certificate for attendees

Free Goodies: Developer bag, T-Shirt, magazines etc.

Exclusive networking events

For further information on the International PHP Conference Munich visit:
https://phpconference.com/munich/

Join us for the 19th Annual Web Developer Conference, PHP Tek 2027, April 27-29 2026.

PHP Tek combines leadership, expertise, and networking in one event. A relaxing atmosphere for tech leaders and developers to share, learn and grow professionally while also providing you with the knowledge to solve your everyday problems.

We are the longest-running web developer conference in the United States, focusing on the PHP programming language. The event is broken up into multiple days. The main conference happens over the course of 3 days (April 27-29) and includes keynotes, talks, and networking options. It will be broken into three tracks and will cover a range of topics. There will be two dedicated PHP Tracks, and then each day will have a different 3rd track (JS/Laravel/DevOps)

Head over to https://phptek.io and get yours today!

The
PHP Velho Oeste
is a national-level conference that takes place annually in the West of Santa Catarina, Brazil,
known as Velho Oeste(Old West).

Knowledge + Networking

In this event, several relevant topics will be covered, from the latest language updates to best
development practices. You will have the opportunity to expand your PHP knowledge and stay up to date
with the latest market trends.

Date: May 29-30, 2025

Location: Unochapecó Noble Hall in Chapecó, Santa Catarina, Brazil.
